title: perf(state): skip unchanged scalar writes and resolve stale computed vars lazily
author: FarhanAliRaza
awaiting: maintainer review (masenf raised a behavior-change concern in comments; author says it was dropped)

unresolved.first_comment: P1 Failed recomputation loses stale state: when a stale computed getter raises, _resolve_stale has already removed its stale marker while leaving the old cache intact, so subsequent reads treat the outdated cached value as current

P1 Keep dynamically added dependencies in the forward map: add_dependency() after class init updates _var_dependencies but not _computed_var_deps, so _resolve_stale() sees no forward deps and returns without recomputing
P2 Skip dependencies already resolved from the stale snapshot: dependent before dependency in the set snapshot causes the dependency getter to be recomputed twice
P2 Preserve the sign when comparing zero-valued floats: 0.0 == -0.0 so assigning one over the other returns early under the scalar cutoff

P1: When a cached synchronous ComputedVar receives a dependency through add_dependency() after class initialization, this reverse map never includes it. The stale resolver retains the old cache and omits the computed value from the delta
P2: If a stale computed getter raises, this method has already removed its stale marker, so the cached old value is returned on the next read without retrying

outstanding_asks.ask: The scalar self-assignment cutoff is a behavior change that breaks apps using self-assignment to force a computed-var cascade; the API to mark vars dirty explicitly is not nice enough to be the fallback.
outstanding_asks.evidence: Author replied 'droped that' at 19:02Z and a commit titled 'Drop the scalar write cutoff' (fc47df9) is referenced by greptile; the PR title/body still describe the cutoff though.
